genZNote: The unsung hero of sauerkraut and kimchi's first fermentation stage, and the industrial source of dextran, the sugar polymer used in blood plasma substitutes and chromatography beads.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Plant surfaces, fermenting vegetables, and dairy
habitat.hostAssociation: Not part of normal human microbiota; used as a food-fermentation starter organism
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Naturally initiates fermentation of sauerkraut, kimchi, and some cheeses; industrially cultured for dextran production
habitat.reservoir: Plant surfaces and fermenting food environments

culture.growthCharacteristics: Facultative anaerobe; produces large, mucoid, dextran-slime colonies on sucrose-containing media
culture.colonyMorphology: Large, mucoid, glistening colonies from dextran slime production on sucrose media

biochemicalTests.test: Heterofermentative glucose fermentation (CO2, ethanol, lactic acid)

identificationClues: Heterofermentative metabolism — produces CO2, ethanol, and lactic acid from glucose, unlike the purely lactic-acid-producing homofermentative lactobacilli
Produces copious extracellular dextran (a glucose polymer) when grown on sucrose, giving colonies a distinctive mucoid, slimy appearance
Initiates the first stage of vegetable fermentations like sauerkraut and kimchi, later succeeded by more acid-tolerant lactobacilli
Industrially cultured specifically for dextran production, used in blood plasma volume expanders and chromatography resin manufacturing

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Catalase negative; heterofermentative (CO2 + ethanol + lactic acid)
examFacts.importantDisease: None — food fermentation and industrial dextran-production organism
examFacts.importantTest: Mucoid dextran-slime colonies on sucrose media
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Heterofermentative starter of vegetable fermentations (sauerkraut, kimchi) and the industrial source of dextran
